question.text: The premium for currency options shall be quoted in:

answer.text: Indian Rupees (for INR-based options) and quote currency for cross-currency options
Always in the base currency of the pair

explanation.text: The Logic: INR-based currency option premiums are quoted in Indian rupees. For cross-currency option contracts, EURUSD and GBPUSD option premiums are quoted in USD, while USDJPY option premiums are quoted in JPY. The Trap: The premium currency follows the convention specified for each contract, not a single global rule like "always USD" or "always percentage of contract value". Note: The premium quotation convention is set out on pages 87-89 of the NISM Series-I workbook. The USDINR lot-size arithmetic (e.g., Rs. 0.10 per unit times 1,000 lot = Rs. 100 total premium per lot) is consistent with the workbook contract-value table.
